subject: Service retainer, TAM coverage, and incident notification protocol
messages:
From: Sam Walker <sam.walker@firsthorizon.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@firsthorizon.com
Date: 2026-11-27T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: RFP: TAM coverage / retainer questions

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement has a few follow-ups we need answered for the RFP record related to support hours and escalation commitments if we proceed with a paid retainer:

- What is the standard TAM on-call schedule for a 24x7 retainer? How many named individuals and fallback contacts?
- For a sev-1 incident, what is your guaranteed response time for acknowledgement vs. time-to-restore SLAs (or typical target)?
- How do you notify customers during an incident (channels, cadence, and who is the primary contact on our side)?
- Do you provide a separate escalation matrix and a sample runbook for joint incident comms?

If you can send a short doc and the names/titles of the primary TAMs assigned under a retainer, procurement will add that to the packet. We also need to know what evidence (SLA reports, audit logs) you can provide for monthly reviews.

Appreciate it — we have an internal deadline on Friday.

Sam
Sam Walker
Director, Cloud Ops — First Horizon Bank
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Sam Walker <sam.walker@firsthorizon.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-28T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: RFP: TAM coverage / retainer questions

Sam —

Thanks for the questions and the deadline. Attached are two artifacts to start: a short SOW for a TAM retainer and an escalation matrix template. High level answers inline below; please let me know if you want a 20-minute call to walk through.

- TAM on-call schedule: For a 24x7 retainer we name two primary TAMs and one rota backup (3 total). Primary TAMs rotate on a two-week cadence and provide handoff notes.
- Response vs restore: Acknowledgement for sev-1 incidents is within 15 minutes during retainer hours (24x7) and a targeted mitigation/update cadence every 30 minutes until resolution. Time-to-restore targets depend on incident class and root cause; we commit to a communication SLA (acknowledge + 30-min updates) and an operational playbook for remediation steps.
- Notifications: We support email, SMS, PagerDuty, and a dedicated webhook to your incident management. Primary notification will go to your ops distribution list and to the named TAMs. We will also provide a customer-facing incident timeline post-resolution.
- Evidence for monthly reviews: token-level latency/cost reports, per-route error rates, audit logs (API calls), and on-call incident logs. We can share these through a shared Drive folder and periodic PDF reports.

Attachments: Redwood_TAM_Retainer_SOW_v1.pdf; Escalation_Matrix.xlsx

Next steps: If this aligns, I can draft the retainer exhibit and send a DocuSign link for signatures.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
